Patched libsql_experimental.a for linux/amd64

Why: the upstream go-libsql archive (libsql-0.9.25) closes each local
sqlite3 handle twice on connection teardown (LibsqlConnection::drop and
then Connection::drop both call Connection::disconnect). The second
sqlite3_close_v2 reads freed memory and intermittently crashes with
SIGSEGV. Upstream issue: https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql/issues/2251
Upstream fix:   https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql/pull/2261 (commit 4e06af572ddf)
As of 2026-11-09 the latest go-libsql (3051e37e6e04) still ships the
unfixed archive, so it is rebuilt here.

Source:   tursodatabase/libsql tag libsql-0.9.25 (d4026bcc69c8bbfdcf301b2c438c98856ce54980)
Patch:    ../../patches/0001-null-sqlite3-handle-after-close.patch (only change)
Crate:    bindings/c (sql-experimental), cargo build --release --locked
Image:    ghcr.io/cross-rs/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:0.2.5 (same as upstream's `cross`)
Toolchain: rustc 1.85.0 (4d91de4e4 2025-02-17), cargo 1.85.0, gcc 5.4.0, glibc 2.23
Rebuild:  ../../patches/build-linux-amd64.sh (see header comment for docker command)

sha256 patched:  a3501069e83ef0379b3354aed06a5bfe6deb67bc33551273610ae416c2989d4a
sha256 original: 5d46b9ab4c38aa7ed6567fe8a75d8619f0b35183b588bbd6786c08c7a8a33581

Compatibility checks against the original archive: lib/include/libsql.h is
byte-identical, the exported libsql_* symbol set is identical, and the set of
glibc-version-sensitive undefined symbols is identical.

Not patched: lib/linux_arm64 and lib/darwin_arm64 are the original upstream
archives and still contain the double-close bug.
